name: South Seas Mandate
alt: Mandated Territory of the South Sea Islands

predecessors.name: German New Guinea
predecessors.text: 'the Micronesian islands north of the equator, formerly part of German New Guinea': the Marianas, Carolines, Marshall Islands and Palau

successors.name: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands
successors.text: the same islands: 'The League of Nations mandate was formally revoked by the United Nations on 18 July 1947'; the United States became responsible 'under a trusteeship that established the Trust…

ledger.x: 1920: Japan receives the League of Nations mandate for the South Seas Islands: 'a League of Nations mandate given to the Empire of Japan by the League of Nations following World War I' (infobox 'Class C League of Nations mandate of Japan (1920-1947)').
1921: the Civil Affairs Bureau, 'initially based in Truk', 'moved to Koror in the Palau islands in 1921'.

1932: the South Seas Government (Nan'yō-chō) is set up: 'The establishment of the South Seas Government or Nan'yō-chō in March 1932 finally put the government of the islands under a purely civilian administration.'
1944: the Marshall Islands campaign opens (31 January 1944): the Majuro landing 'marked the beginning of Operation Flintlock, the invasion of Kwajalein'.
1944: the Marshall Islands campaign ends in February: Kwajalein was captured on 7 February and the whole of Eniwetok atoll 'by 23 February'; 'This marked an end to the Marshall Islands campaign.'
1944: the United States holds the Marshall Islands from February 1944.
1944: the Mariana Islands campaign opens: 'Battle of Saipan, 15 June - 9 July 1944'; Tinian 24 July to 1 August 1944.
1944: the Marianas are secured: 'After heavy fighting, Saipan was secured in July and Guam and Tinian in August 1944.'

1944: the United States holds the Northern Mariana Islands from August 1944 ('Saipan was secured in July and Guam and Tinian in August 1944'); the smaller islands to the north are not dated on the page.
1944: the Palau campaign opens: 'Battle of Peleliu, 15 September - 27 November 1944'; Angaur 17 September to 22 October 1944.
1944: Peleliu and Angaur are secured: 'both islands were finally secured by U.S. forces in November 1944'; Koror 'was bypassed altogether, only to surrender in August 1945'.

1945: the bypassed islands pass to American occupation at Japan's capitulation: the Palau page says the Koror garrison 'was bypassed altogether, only to surrender in August 1945 with the Japan's capitulation'; the same is the researcher's reading for Truk, Yap, Pohnpei and Kosrae.
1947: the American occupation of the Marshall Islands ends as the trusteeship begins (18 July 1947).
1947: the American occupation of the Mariana Islands of the mandate ends as the trusteeship begins (18 July 1947).
1947: the American occupation of the Palau Islands and the Caroline Islands ends as the trusteeship begins (18 July 1947).

ledger.cpn: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands

wars.name: Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign
wars.outcome: Majuro and Kwajalein (from 31 January 1944; Kwajalein captured 7 February) and Eniwetok (17 to 23 February 1944): 'This marked an end to the Marshall Islands campaign.'

wars.name: Mariana and Palau Islands campaign
wars.outcome: Saipan 15 June to 9 July, Tinian 24 July to 1 August, Guam 21 July to 10 August (American territory, retaken); Peleliu 15 September to 27 November, Angaur 17 September to 22 October 1944.

certainty.note: Islands: the border is the coast and the mandate's limit at the equator; Guam's exclusion is a fact of American sovereignty.
